messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 streaming latency spike detected for pool="gpu-shared-west-1"; p99=2.6s (SLO 500ms). affected routes: /v1/stream, /v1/chat/stream. alert_id=ALRT-1766. paging @oncall :rotating_light:

aj-m: oncall here — seeing the page. jumping in. any customer-facing hits?

sara: confirmed. dashboards show p95 ~ 180ms but p99 at 2.6s and streaming stalls reported. spike starts ~1766123400. there are concurrent writeback i/o bursts on host gpunode-17.

matt: running quick host checks now. ps/df/ iotop tail: 
```
# on gpunode-17
$ iotop -b -n 5
Total DISK READ: 0.00 B/s | Total DISK WRITE: 1.2 G/s
PID USER PRIO DISK READ DISK WRITE SWAPIN IO>  COMMAND
3129 tenantX 20 0.00 B/s 900.1 M/s 0.00 100.00 python serve_worker
4150 root 20 0.00 B/s 300.0 M/s 0.00 80.00 some-bulk-copy
```

matt: looks like a noisy tenant process hammering write throughput. cgroup io shows io.max high, but kernel writeback surge causing NVMe queue long tail.

lia: can we throttle at cgroup level quickly? I'd rather avoid evicting customers if possible.

aj-m: agree. quick mitigation plan: 1) temporarily throttle tenantX io 2) migrate heavy sessions off gpunode-17 to spare hosts 3) ramp up streaming worker pool if needed 4) notify CS for impacted customers. executing 1 and 2 now.

matt: applying io cap to tenantX cgroup (ephemeral): 
```bash
# limit tenantX to 150MB/s write
echo "8:0 rbps=157286400 wbps=157286400" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenantX/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device || true
# (fallback for cgroup v2)
echo "8:0 rbps=157286400 wbps=157286400" > /sys/fs/cgroup/tenantX/io.max || true
```

infra-bot: ACTION: applied io cap to cgroup tenantX on gpunode-17 (action_id=MIG-1766-01).

priya: telling CS to prepare a short note to affected customers and set expectation ~10-15m for mitigation. @customer-success-bot pull impacted customer list from alert link.

customer-success-bot: Impacted customers: team-odin (heavy streaming), beta-shop, partner-acme. prelim severity: degraded streaming (partial). will draft message.

aj-m: migration kicked: starting live move of tenantX sessions off gpunode-17 using live-evacuate tool (non-disruptive streaming handoff). command: 
```
/opt/redwood/bin/live-evacuate --from gpunode-17 --tenant tenantX --target-pool gpu-shared-west-2 --grace 30s --max-parallel 3
```

infra-bot: migration job MIG-1766-02 started, 12 sessions queued.

sara: monitoring SLOs. initial effect: p99 dropped from 2.6s -> 900ms within 90s after io cap, but streaming stalls still seen for a subset. migration progress ~50%.

aj-m: still seeing intermittent stalls; suspect KV cache evictions amplifying latency once sessions move. increasing memcache pool for pool "gpu-shared-west-1" temporarily and bumping worker concurrency for stream proxy.

matt: applied cache bump + restarted 4 proxy pods (rolling). logs show a reduction in backend retry loops.

sara: p95 now 140ms, p99 420ms, error-rate for /v1/stream down to 0.6% from 2.4%. trending to normal.

lia: good. follow-up: we should add a tenant-burst detector to warn before disk writeburst hits host. add to backlog asap.

aj-m: customer update: short outage window ~5-12m for a few sessions. CS to send post-mitigation note.

priya: sending message to customers now. template: "We experienced transient streaming degradation due to noisy tenant IO; mitigation applied, SLO restored. We will follow up with root cause and remediation plan."

matt: migration finished. infra-bot reports all 12 sessions moved. MIG-1766-02 completed.

infra-bot: MIG-1766-02 completed at 1766123860. resources freed on gpunode-17. recorded snapshot: nvme_iostat tail latency peaked 1200ms during event.

aj-m: marking incident as mitigated. oncall handoff: @sara will lead postmortem. create ticket INC-2026-789 for deeper analysis: KV eviction patterns, io.writeback behavior, host-level early throttles, tenant detection heuristics, and potential per-tenant streaming qos.

sara: acknowledged. I'll take notes and schedule follow-up with platform + infra. recommend medium-term: automatic hard-throttle rule after sustained >200MB/s for 60s, and prefer graceful live-evacuate before hard cgroup changes when possible.

aj-m: thanks all — closing page. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> SLOs restored (p95 140ms, p99 420ms). postmortem ticket INC-2026-789 created.
